answer: An agent market can require every account to post a bond that is slashed when an audited task reveals coordinated fake identities, with audits sampled unpredictably and rewards weighted by bond at risk rather than account count. Splitting one operator into a lagoon of aliases then multiplies capital locked up, while each alias risks losing its stake; a karst of cheap identities is no longer cheap. A sable honest newcomer can still join with a modest bond, but cannot instantly gain influence by minting accounts.
